==English== {{wp|+ and no}} ===Etymology=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:yes>>>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|yes}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ġīese|t=by all means, of course, yes}}, derived from the same root as {{m|en|yea}}. Compare {{cog|fo|júsá|t=yes, indeed, certainly}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/jɛs/|a=RP,GA,CA}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-yes.ogg|a=UK}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-yes.wav|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|En-us-yes.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|En-nz-yes.ogg|a=NZ|IPA=[jɪi̯s]}} * {{IPA|en|/jɪs/|a=obsolete}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛs|s=1}} ===Particle=== {{en-head|pcl}} # {{non-gloss|Used to show [[agree]]ment or acceptance.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Yes''', you are correct.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Yes''', you may go play outside now.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Yes''', sir, we have your package right here.}} # {{non-gloss|Used to indicate ''disagreement'' or ''dissent'' in reply to a negative statement.}} #: {{ux|en|It was not my fault we lost the race.
Oh, '''yes''', it was!}} # {{lb|en|humorous}} {{n-g|Answer to a question presuming one answer when all answers are correct.}} #: {{ux|en|Do you like cake, or pie?
'''Yes'''.}} #: {{rfquote-sense|en}} (Countless examples can be found on the [https://www.reddit.com/r/InclusiveOr/ “Inclusive Or” subreddit], which is a [[forum]] dedicated to this joke.) ====Usage notes==== * In Old and Middle English, ''yes'' was a more forceful affirmative than {{m|en|yea}}. * An example of '''yes''' used to disagree with a statement: the questions "You don’t want it, do you?" and "Don’t you want it?" are answered by "yes" if the respondent ''does'' want the item, and "no" if not. Many languages use a specific word for this purpose; see translation table below. ====Synonyms==== * Dialect or archaic forms: [[arr]], [[ay]], [[aye]], [[yea]], [[yassuh]] * Nautical, military, telecommunications: [[affirmative]] * Colloquial or slang forms: [[ya]], [[yah]], [[yeah]], [[yeh]], [[yep]], [[yeppers]], [[yup]], [[yuppers]], [[yus]], [[ahuh]], [[mhm]], [[uh huh]], [[ye-es]] * See also: [[Thesaurus:yes]] ====Antonyms==== * Standard form: [[no]] * Nautical, military, telecommunications: [[negative]] * Dialect or archaic forms: [[nay]] * Colloquial or slang forms: [[ixnay]],
